paper.central_claim: ERL reflects on single-attempt task trajectories and outcomes to write trigger-conditioned heuristics into a persistent pool, retrieves the most relevant ones with an LLM at test time and injects them into the agent's system prompt; on Gaia2 (Search and Execution) it improves success by 7.8 points over a ReAct baseline, outperforms ExpeL and AutoGuide, selective retrieval is essential, and heuristics transfer better than raw few-shot trajectories.
paper.title: Experiential Reflective Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents

gap.author_gap: Agents approach each new task from scratch; prior experiential methods (ExpeL, AutoGuide) need repeated rollouts or paired trajectories, concatenate all insights into every prompt, or add per-turn retrieval overhead, which breaks down when tasks cannot be retried.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete and plausible deployment gap vs two named neighbors. The scaling-poorly and overhead claims are argued rather than measured, and the reflection-store-retrieve loop is a well-covered family whose other members (Voyager-style, memory-centric agents) are cited in a list but not compared.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion, ExpeL (insight extraction with retries), AutoGuide (context-aware guidelines), plus a cited cluster of experiential-memory works not compared.
gap.residue: Store maintenance (conflicts, consolidation), online accumulation (iterative ERL degrades), scaling retrieval beyond about 20 entries.
gap.stakes: Practical agent deployment without retries or curated training sets.
gap.method_response: Single-attempt reflection into trigger-conditioned heuristics plus LLM retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: Maintenance, online learning, and generality beyond Gaia2 (tau2-bench shows no passˆ3 gain).
unresolved: Comparison to other experiential-memory systems at matched experience budgets

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A pool of heuristics distilled from single-attempt trajectories on 8 Gaia2 universes raises success on 2 held-out universes by about 5 to 8 points over ReAct (GPT-5-mini; 76 tasks, 3 runs), and raw few-shot trajectories do not help; the gain is not shown to beat retry-based baselines at matched experience budgets, retrieval adds about 2 points over random selection, and the online accumulation loop and the second benchmark do not reproduce the gain.
unresolved: Opus: k and retriever selected on the test universes (opus:O01).
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; nothing was run by us. 'Retained' reflects held-out-universe gains from a frozen pool; no improver-level claim is made or supported.
assessment.evidence_level_note: A pool frozen after accumulation on 8 universes is read on 2 disjoint universes, with a store-off (ReAct) control. Test-tuned k/retriever is charged in E.holdout, not by lowering the level (SWE-Exp precedent).

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. A concrete deployment gap relative to ExpeL and AutoGuide (retries, paired trajectories, all-insight prompts, per-turn retrieval). The overhead claims are argued, and other experiential-memory systems are only cited.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Single-attempt post-mortem → trigger/action guideline → LLM relevance retrieval, tested against distinguishable naive alternatives (raw trajectories, random, embedding).

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Formats, prompts, k and injection are reproducible. There is no admission gate, maintenance, conflict handling or versioning, and the online variant degrades.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Gaia2 ground-truth trajectories with automatic verification, plus pass@3/pass^3. The ARE judge shares the agent's model and is not audited.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Store-off, random, embedding, token-matched raw trajectories and source-kind controls are present. But ExpeL/AutoGuide experience budgets are unmatched (opus:O03), the GPT-5.2 ranker is stronger than the baselines' retrievers, random heuristics give most of the gain (opus:O04), and failures-only exceeds the headline.

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with sol. Accumulation and test use disjoint universes and τ²-bench train/test, which is real hold-out of the store content. But k and the retriever are chosen from sweeps on the test universes (headline = best cell, opus:O01), the retrieval prompt was hand-selected, and there are only two test universes. son55's 3 names the test tuning but does not charge it; its own local-1 is 'unmet'.

E.statistics.reason: Opus sides with sol (A2 ladder): pass^3/pass@3 over three runs are repeated-run failure counts, and sample sizes and negative results are reported. There are no intervals or tests, and margins between variants are about 2 points on 76 tasks.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with son55. Appendix D gives per-phase input/output tokens, cache share and dollars for baseline vs ERL (+40% overall), and C.1 adds a token-matched few-shot comparison, which is real budget-fairness evidence against the cheapest alternative. Source-trajectory rollouts are not an extra cost under the paper's deployment framing, since tasks are run anyway. Not 4: retry-based baselines are not costed or budget-matched, and latency is unmeasured.
